summary: Exactly the mirror image of 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD--- with states A and D exchanged (that machine's table started in state D): long blocks of 3-cell words and a final block of a 9-cell word changed by the same five kinds of phase (periods proved in Lean, drain for the twin only); an exact accelerated simulation reaches 1.06e300 steps without a halt.
title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1LA0LD_1LB0LF_0RB0LE_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1LA0LD_1LB0LF_0RB0LE_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. This machine is the mirror image of 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD--- with states A and D exchanged, so its run is that table started in state D. One period of four of its five kinds of phase is proved in Lean for all block lengths (kernel; the fifth, drain, is kernel-checked for the twin only); an exact accelerated simulation, checked against direct simulation, follows the run to 1.06·10300 steps without a halt (trusted). How a phase ends depends on residues of the counts.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,812 cells have been visited and 19,072 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.57).

claims.title: Traverse, one cycle
claims.text: 0^∞ A>0 1 1 (010110110)^(p+1) (110)^(q+1) (010)^(r+1) (110)^(s+1) 1 1 1 (011)^(t+6) 0 1 0^∞ reaches the same with p+2, s+7, t in 396p + 132q + 132r + 132s + 1363 steps (nine visits of the left end), for every p, q, r, s, t.

claims.title: Mirror twin
claims.text: Reflecting 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD--- (L and R swapped) and renaming A to D and D to A gives this machine's table exactly; its start state A is the twin's D. Checked by a script comparing the two tables under all relabellings (only this one matches).

claims.title: Five phase periods
claims.text: One period of four of the five kinds of phase the run uses after step 10<sup>20</sup> (mirror images of the twin's): cross (marker moves 6 words, final block +1), two double crossings, absorb (right block +4, neighbour −2), feed (middle block −18, right block +30, final +1), each for every value of its variables. The drain period (final block −11, marker 18 words, new block +36) is not in Lean here: its generated proof needs more than 9 GB of memory; the mirror-image period is kernel-checked for the twin.

claims.title: No halt in 1.06·10<sup>300</sup> steps
claims.text: The twin's exact accelerated simulator (with crossings of long blocks also counted as events, ACCEL_X=1), compared with direct C simulation after every jump up to 1.08·1010 steps with no mismatch, reaches 1.06·10300 steps (401 drain phases) without a halt; the tape grows 1.98 to 4.01 times per drain phase (median 2.23).

claims.title: Drain period
claims.text: Final block −11, a marker moves 18 words, a new block +36 per period: verified by the symbolic run of the accelerated simulator for all block lengths, not by Lean (memory).

claims.title: Round maps
claims.text: The same two residue-chosen round maps as the twin (see its page), mirrored.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The phase periods are proved; their ends, which depend on residues of the counts, are known from simulation only.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine is the mirror image of another holdout with two states renamed, started in a different state. Its tape is a handful of long blocks; in each phase a marker crawls through a block or a block eats its neighbour, and when a block runs out the next phase starts. An exact fast-forward simulation has followed it for 10<sup>300</sup> steps without a halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.57).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,812 cells (9,917 left of the start, 19,053 right), with a density of 1s of 0.548.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A mirror image, started elsewhere
html: Take 1RB0RF_1RC0LD_1RD0RA_1LB1LE_0LB0RE_0RD---, swap every L and R, and rename state A to D and D to A. The result is this machine's table, entry for entry:

Both start on a blank tape, but this one starts in the twin's state D, so the two runs are different orbits of the same dynamics. They use the same kinds of phase, mirrored: the final block of 9-cell words sits at the left end here.

sections.heading: Long blocks and a final block
html: At the left end (state E) the tape reads like 0 0 0 (101101100)^509 (101)^4551 (100)^856 (101)^5329 (110)^10179 1 (step 3,039,097,886): a final block of the 9-cell word 101101100, then long blocks of 3-cell words.

sections.heading: Five kinds of phase
html:
phaseper periodLean
crossa marker moves 6 words right; final block +1cross6
drainfinal block −11; a marker moves 18 words; a new block +36twin only
double crosstwo markers move 12 words; final block +1cross12, cross12b
absorbat the right end: right block +4, its neighbour −2absorb2
feedat the right end: a middle block −18, right block +30, final block +1feed30

Each row but drain is a Lean theorem here for every value of the block lengths (drain is proved for the twin; here its proof is too large to check). A phase lasts until a shrinking block is too short; the remainder decides the junction the next phase starts from. The twin's page describes the resulting round maps (two branches, chosen by residues).

sections.heading: Fast-forwarding exactly
html: The twin's simulator proves each period symbolically and applies it many times at once, so it reproduces the machine's tape and step count exactly (checked against plain simulation up to 1010 steps). For this run it also counts the crossing of a long block as an event, because here the head spends long stretches zig-zagging inside the tape.
No halt so far. The only halting transition is F reading a 1; F is entered only from D reading a 1, and in every proved phase that cell is 0.
